candidates.attacker_control: The final path segment of the request URI (e.g. GET /context/<action>/<id>/<attacker-method>), taken from RequestUtils.getUri(request) (servletPath/requestURI, container-decoded) via RestActionMapper.getMapping (line 185) and stored verbatim as ActionMapping.method at line 220. The method string is subsequently OGNL-evaluated at DefaultActionInvocation.java:430.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that the sibling '!' handler does enforce allowDynamicMethodCalls and cleanupActionName (RestActionMapper.java:313-317) - showing the omission at 219-220 is an inconsistency, not an intentional global policy. Verified that isAllowedMethod's wildcard is the default (ActionConfig.java:137-143 and embalmTarget 346-356) and that struts-default.xml defines no allowed-methods/strict-method-invocation, so the guard usually does not block. Verified that cleanupActionName is available in the same class but not applied here. Checked default.properties (DMI false, action-prefix disabled) and the fact that the method name is only reached from the URI path, not from request parameters, so container URI decoding/validation is a partial constraint on injectable characters. Considered that the generic DMI paths (DefaultActionMapper.parseActionName / method: prefix) are correctly gated, so the issue is specific to RestActionMapper's URL-path branch.
candidates.impact: Bypass of the struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation restriction: a remote, unauthenticated request can cause invocation of action methods that were intended to be reachable only through explicit configuration (for example state-changing or administrative methods on the action), and because the attacker-chosen method string is fed to OGNL evaluation under the value stack, it is an expression-injection primitive of the same class historically used for RCE in this plugin (potential remote code execution depending on OGNL sandbox and available action methods). No runtime confirmation was performed.
candidates.prerequisites: REST plugin present (its struts-plugin.xml sets struts.mapper.class=rest, line 45) and an action reachable in the mapped namespace; struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation=false (the framework default, default.properties:109); the target action has no explicit <allowed-methods> and its package does not set strict-method-invocation, so ActionConfig.allowedMethods is the wildcard '*'. (If an application explicitly configures allowed-methods/strict-method-invocation, isAllowedMethod rejects unknown names and blocks this path.)
candidates.root_cause: RestActionMapper.getMapping derives the action method from the last URI path segment and calls mapping.setMethod(...) unconditionally (RestActionMapper.java:219-220). The parallel '!method' path is gated by allowDynamicMethodCalls and sanitized with cleanupActionName() (RestActionMapper.java:313-317), but this path neither checks struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation nor sanitizes the method name, so the DMI-off configuration is bypassed. The value is later passed to DefaultActionProxy.prepare -> ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod(), which returns true for every method when no <allowed-methods> is configured (wildcard inserted by ActionConfig.Builder.embalmTarget, ActionConfig.java:346-356; struts-default.xml defines no allowed-methods/strict-method-invocation), and finally to DefaultActionInvocation.invokeAction, which evaluates the string as an OGNL expression: ognlUtil.getValue(methodName + "()", getStack().getContext(), action) (DefaultActionInvocation.java:430).
candidates.title: REST plugin ActionMapper invokes arbitrary method names from the URL path when Dynamic Method Invocation is disabled, with the method name evaluated as OGNL
candidates.trace: HTTP request URI -> RestActionMapper.getMapping (lines 181-296) -> parseNameAndNamespace (name cleaned) -> handleDynamicMethodInvocation only gates the '!' convention -> lines 212-225: prevSlashPos > -1 && method == null -> mapping.setMethod(fullName.substring(lastSlashPos+1)) with no allowDynamicMethodCalls check and no cleanupActionName -> Returned ActionMapping.method -> DefaultActionProxy.prepare (lines 188-192) -> ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod true via wildcard -> DefaultActionInvocation.invokeAction line 430 ognlUtil.getValue(methodName + "()", stack context, action) -> arbitrary action-method invocation and OGNL expression evaluation.
candidates.unverified: No execution/testing: whether a concrete OGNL payload survives URI decoding and the value stack's SecurityMemberAccess restrictions was not established; only source-level reachability of OGNL evaluation of an attacker-chosen method string is shown. Whether this exact branch is the one changed by the upstream fix could not be confirmed from the snapshot; behavior of the servlet container's path decoding is environment-dependent.
candidates.weakness_type: Dynamic method invocation bypass leading to OGNL expression evaluation / expression injection (CWE-749, CWE-917)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned Struts 2.3.29-SNAPSHOT tree (4414 files). Focus areas: core dispatcher/filter and action mapping (Dispatcher, PrepareOperations, StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter, DefaultActionMapper, PrefixBasedActionMapper), xwork-core action invocation and config (DefaultActionProxy/Factory, DefaultActionInvocation, ActionConfig, XmlConfigurationProvider), OGNL/localization utilities (OgnlUtil, OgnlValueStack, SecurityMemberAccess, TextParseUtil, LocalizedTextUtil, DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker), interceptors (Parameters, Cookie, FileUpload, Debugging, Multiselect, I18n), multipart parsers (Jakarta/JakartaStream/MultiPartRequestWrapper), and the REST plugin (RestActionMapper, RestActionInvocation, RestWorkflowInterceptor, struts-plugin.xml, tests). Also spot-checked showcase actions and the REST showcase configuration. The P1 relation index covers only 228 of 2085 Java files with no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution and 25 parse errors, so index gaps most of the tree; statements about unindexed areas rely on direct source reads only, and large areas (most apps/plugins, JSP/Freemarker/Velocity templates, OSGi/portlet/embedded JSP, most tests) were not exhaustively reviewed.
limitations: No code execution, builds, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were run; all conclusions are source-reading only.

External dependencies (commons-fileupload 1.3.1, OGNL 3.0.14, servlet container) were not available/inspectable, so exception-message contents, URI decoding, and sandbox behavior are reasoned from source and public vulnerability history, not verified.
P1 index is partial (228/2085 Java files parsed; no data-flow/CFG; 25 parse errors) and its edges are syntactic candidates only; unindexed code may contain the actual target.
The exact upstream fix commit for this snapshot could not be consulted (no history/patches available), so the candidate-to-CVE mapping is an inference from version and code state, not confirmed.
Impact beyond arbitrary method invocation (i.e., actual RCE) depends on OGNL SecurityMemberAccess bypass conditions and on which methods the deployed actions expose; not demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: OGNL evaluation of attacker-influenced default messages: JakartaMultiPartRequest/MultiPartRequestWrapper pass multipart exception text (e.getMessage(), influenced by the Content-Type header) as defaultMessage into LocalizedTextUtil.findText (JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:118-124, MultiPartRequestWrapper.java:106-112), and LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage evaluates the default message through TextParseUtil.translateVariables (LocalizedTextUtil.java:668-690), the mechanism behind the S2-045/S2-046 RCE.
rejected_leads.reason: Real dangerous pattern and clearly present, but treated as a separate root cause from the selected candidate; the snapshot version (2.3.29-SNAPSHOT) predates the upstream fix window for this issue, attacker control over the exception text resides in the external commons-fileupload dependency (not inspectable in this tree), and only one candidate may be submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: Showcase FileDownloadAction serves ServletContext resources based on a request parameter and sanitizeInputPath only rejects names containing 'WEB-INF' (apps/showcase/.../FileDownloadAction.java:41-63).
rejected_leads.reason: Limited to webapp-local resources through ServletContext.getResourceAsStream, is a sample application, and a sanitizer plus unit test (FileDownloadActionTest) already exist in the snapshot; no strong security impact established.

rejected_leads.lead: DebuggingInterceptor 'command' mode evaluates an 'expression' request parameter as OGNL (DebuggingInterceptor.java:189-200).
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only when struts.devMode is enabled (line 149); devMode is false by default (default.properties:140), and the console is documented as a development feature.

rejected_leads.reason: In this snapshot the cookie name is validated against ExcludedPatternsChecker and an accepted-name pattern ('[a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_\'\s]+', line 172/240-289) before injection, and the value is not OGNL-evaluated; no bypass of that check was established.

summary:
Snapshot is Apache Struts 2.3.29-SNAPSHOT (4414 files; core, xwork-core, apps, plugins). Coverage was framework-focused: dispatcher/filter mapping, multipart handling, OGNL utilities/localization, interceptors, and the REST plugin. P1 relation index is partial (228/2085 Java files parsed; no control/data-flow, no semantic resolution, 25 parse errors), so it was used only for navigation; every cited edge was verified in source text.

Strongest candidate: a Dynamic Method Invocation (DMI) bypass in the REST plugin. RestActionMapper.getMapping copies an arbitrary method name from the request URI path into ActionMapping.method (RestActionMapper.java:212-225, especially 219-220) without consulting the allowDynamicMethodCalls flag and without the cleanupActionName() sanitization that the sibling "!method" handler applies (RestActionMapper.java:298-317). DefaultActionInvocation then evaluates the attacker-supplied method name as an OGNL expression ("methodName + \"()\"", DefaultActionInvocation.java:430), and the per-action guard is ineffective by default because ActionConfig.Builder adds a wildcard allowed-methods entry when no <allowed-methods>/strict-method-invocation is configured (ActionConfig.java:137-143, 346-356) — struts-default.xml defines neither. Result: /<action>/<id>/<method> can invoke arbitrary action methods (and attempt OGNL expression injection) even though struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation is false by default; this is the class of issue fixed in the REST plugin in the 2.3.29 timeframe. Confidence medium: no runtime confirmation, and OGNL sandbox / container URI decoding were not exercisable here.

Other plausible-but-not-selected leads are listed in rejected_leads.
